ANEURYSM.rationale: Smoking is the dominant modifiable risk.

DEMENTIA.clue: Several diseases destroy cortex or subcortical circuits

GUILLAIN.clue: Immune attack on peripheral myelin follows campylobacter or another trigger

BOTULISM.clue: The toxin prevents vesicle release at the neuromuscular junction

TORSEMIDE.rationale: This drug is used for edema. Monitor weight, electrolytes, and blood pressure.

HCTZ.clue: Mechanism and effect: thiazide diuretic that can lower potassium and raise uric acid and glucose
HCTZ.rationale: Hydrochlorothiazide is a first-line hypertension option. It is less effective when GFR is very low.

METOLAZONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: thiazide-like diuretic added to a loop for diuretic resistance
METOLAZONE.rationale: This drug is given before the loop dose in sequential nephron blockade. Electrolytes can fall quickly.

METOPROLOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: beta-1 blocker used for heart failure, angina, and rate control
METOPROLOL.rationale: This drug succinate, not the tartrate salt, is the heart-failure evidence formulation. Do not stop abruptly.

CARVEDILOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: nonselective beta blocker with alpha blockade used in HFrEF
CARVEDILOL.rationale: This drug is started low and titrated. It can worsen decompensated fluid overload if begun too soon.

BISOPROLOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: beta-1 selective blocker with a mortality benefit in HFrEF
BISOPROLOL.rationale: This drug is one of the evidence-based beta blockers in systolic heart failure.

ATENOLOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: renally cleared beta blocker that is less used as a first hypertension drug
ATENOLOL.rationale: This drug is cleared by the kidney. It can mask tachycardia from hypoglycemia.

PROPRANOLOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: nonselective beta blocker used for tremor, portal hypertension, and thyroid storm symptoms
PROPRANOLOL.rationale: This drug blocks beta-2 as well, so it can provoke bronchospasm. It is lipophilic and enters the brain.

LABETALOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: combined alpha and beta blocker given IV for hypertensive emergency, including in pregnancy
LABETALOL.rationale: This drug lowers pressure without a pure beta-blocker rise in systemic resistance.

AMLODIPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: dihydropyridine calcium blocker whose main nuisance effect is ankle edema
AMLODIPINE.rationale: This drug dilates arteries. The edema is from precapillary vasodilation, not heart failure by itself.

NIFEDIPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: dihydropyridine used for hypertension; immediate-release capsules are avoided for emergencies
NIFEDIPINE.rationale: Immediate-release This drug can cause reflex tachycardia and ischemia. Extended release is the outpatient form.

DILTIAZEM.clue: Mechanism and effect: non-dihydropyridine calcium blocker used for rate control that is avoided in HFrEF
DILTIAZEM.rationale: This drug slows the AV node. It is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and can worsen systolic heart failure.

VERAPAMIL.clue: Mechanism and effect: calcium blocker that slows heart rate and commonly causes constipation
VERAPAMIL.rationale: This drug is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Avoid it with HFrEF and with many simvastatin doses.

DIGOXIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: cardiac glycoside for rate control and symptoms whose toxicity rises when potassium is low
DIGOXIN.rationale: This drug is renally cleared. Nausea, visual changes, and arrhythmias suggest toxicity.

AMIODARONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: iodine-containing antiarrhythmic that can injure lung, thyroid, and liver
AMIODARONE.rationale: This drug has a half-life of many weeks. It inhibits warfarin metabolism and raises digoxin levels.

SOTALOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiarrhythmic beta blocker that prolongs the QT and is started with monitoring
SOTALOL.rationale: This drug is renally cleared. QT prolongation and torsades are the initiation risk.

DOFETILIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: class III antiarrhythmic started in a monitored setting because of torsades
DOFETILIDE.rationale: This drug dose depends on kidney function and the QT interval. Many drugs are contraindicated with it.

FLECAINIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: class Ic antiarrhythmic avoided in structural heart disease
FLECAINIDE.rationale: This drug can be used for atrial fibrillation in a normal heart. It is proarrhythmic after myocardial infarction.

ADENOSINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: very short-acting drug given as a rapid push for stable SVT
ADENOSINE.rationale: This drug briefly blocks the AV node. Warn the patient about chest discomfort and a pause.

ATROPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antimuscarinic first drug for symptomatic bradycardia
ATROPINE.rationale: This drug raises heart rate by blocking vagal tone. It does not help a denervated transplanted heart.

DOPAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: dose-dependent vasopressor and inotrope
DOPAMINE.rationale: Low This drug doses are not renal-protective. Higher doses raise heart rate and vasoconstriction.

DOBUTAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: beta-1 inotrope used in cardiogenic shock
DOBUTAMINE.rationale: This drug increases contractility and can provoke ischemia or arrhythmias.

MILRINONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: pDE-3 inhibitor that is an inotrope and vasodilator
MILRINONE.rationale: This drug is renally cleared and causes hypotension. It is used in advanced heart failure.

VASOPRESSIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: non-catecholamine vasopressor also used to replace ADH
VASOPRESSIN.rationale: This drug is added in vasodilatory shock and treats central diabetes insipidus.

HYDRALAZINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: arterial vasodilator that causes reflex tachycardia and a lupus-like syndrome
HYDRALAZINE.rationale: This drug is often paired with a nitrate in heart failure when ACE inhibitors cannot be used.

ISOSORBIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: nitrate used for angina and heart failure that requires a nitrate-free interval
ISOSORBIDE.rationale: This drug tolerance develops without a daily drug-free interval. It is contraindicated with PDE-5 inhibitors.

SILDENAFIL.clue: Mechanism and effect: pDE-5 inhibitor that is dangerous with nitrates
SILDENAFIL.rationale: This drug is used for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension. Nitrates are contraindicated.

TADALAFIL.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting PDE-5 inhibitor also used for pulmonary hypertension and urinary symptoms
TADALAFIL.rationale: This drug lasts longer than sildenafil. The nitrate interaction window is longer too.

SIMVASTATIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: statin with a dose cap when combined with amlodipine or certain CYP3A4 inhibitors
SIMVASTATIN.rationale: This drug myopathy risk rises with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. High doses are restricted.

PRAVASTATIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: statin not metabolized by CYP3A4, useful when interactions are a concern
PRAVASTATIN.rationale: This drug is hydrophilic and has fewer CYP drug interactions than simvastatin.

EZETIMIBE.clue: Mechanism and effect: cholesterol absorption inhibitor added when statin LDL lowering is not enough
EZETIMIBE.rationale: This drug blocks intestinal cholesterol uptake. It is often combined with a statin.

FENOFIBRATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: fibrate that lowers triglycerides and is preferred over gemfibrozil with a statin
FENOFIBRATE.rationale: This drug has less statin interaction than gemfibrozil, but muscle risk is not zero.

GEMFIBROZIL.clue: Mechanism and effect: fibrate that should not be combined with simvastatin because of rhabdomyolysis
GEMFIBROZIL.rationale: This drug inhibits statin glucuronidation. The combination with simvastatin is contraindicated.

NIACIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: lipid drug that causes flushing, which can be reduced by taking aspirin before it
NIACIN.rationale: This drug raises HDL and can worsen glucose and uric acid. Flushing is prostaglandin mediated.

COLESEVELAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: bile acid sequestrant that lowers LDL and can bind other oral drugs
COLESEVELAM.rationale: This drug is taken with meals and separated from other medications. It can raise triglycerides.

METFORMIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: first-line biguanide for type 2 diabetes that is held around iodinated contrast
METFORMIN.rationale: This drug does not cause hypoglycemia alone. Lactic acidosis risk rises when the kidneys cannot clear it.

GLIPIZIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sulfonylurea that releases insulin and can cause hypoglycemia
GLIPIZIDE.rationale: This drug must be taken with food. Skip the dose if the patient is not eating.

GLYBURIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting sulfonylurea generally avoided in older adults
GLYBURIDE.rationale: This drug causes prolonged hypoglycemia and is on beers-criteria avoidance lists.

GLIMEPIRIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sulfonylurea taken once daily that still carries hypoglycemia risk
GLIMEPIRIDE.rationale: This drug stimulates insulin release. Renal impairment prolongs the effect.

REPAGLINIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: meglitinide taken with meals that is skipped when a meal is skipped
REPAGLINIDE.rationale: This drug has a short action. Gemfibrozil is contraindicated because it markedly raises levels.

SITAGLIPTIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: dPP-4 inhibitor that is weight neutral and rarely causes hypoglycemia alone
SITAGLIPTIN.rationale: This drug dose is reduced in kidney disease. Pancreatitis is a rare warning.

LINAGLIPTIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: dPP-4 inhibitor that does not need renal dose adjustment
LINAGLIPTIN.rationale: This drug is excreted by the bile. It is an option when creatinine clearance is low.

LIRAGLUTIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: daily GLP-1 agonist that helps weight and has a boxed thyroid C-cell warning
LIRAGLUTIDE.rationale: This drug slows gastric emptying. Nausea is common and pancreatitis is a stop-the-drug symptom.

SEMAGLUTIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: gLP-1 agonist available as a weekly injection or an oral tablet taken on an empty stomach
SEMAGLUTIDE.rationale: Oral This drug is taken with a small sip of water and no food for 30 minutes. GI effects are common.

INSULIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: hormone replacement that causes hypoglycemia and is a high-alert medication
INSULIN.rationale: This drug doses are double-checked. Rotate sites and match mealtime This drug to carbohydrate intake.

LISPRO.clue: Mechanism and effect: rapid-acting insulin given with the meal, not long before the tray arrives
LISPRO.rationale: This drug starts within minutes. Giving it and delaying food causes hypoglycemia.

GLARGINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting insulin with no pronounced peak that is not mixed in the same syringe
GLARGINE.rationale: Insulin This drug is usually once daily. Do not mix it with other insulins.

DETEMIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting insulin bound to albumin, dosed once or twice daily
DETEMIR.rationale: Insulin This drug has a relatively flat profile. It is not mixed with other insulins.

NPH.clue: Mechanism and effect: cloudy intermediate insulin with a peak that requires a planned snack or meal
NPH.rationale: This drug is rolled, not shaken. When mixing, it is drawn after the clear short-acting insulin.

METHIMAZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antithyroid drug avoided in the first trimester because of teratogenicity
METHIMAZOLE.rationale: This drug can cause agranulocytosis. Fever or sore throat means stop the drug and check a white count.

PREDNISONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: corticosteroid that must be tapered after long courses and raises glucose
PREDNISONE.rationale: This drug causes infection risk, insomnia, and adrenal suppression. Do not stop a long course abruptly.

ALENDRONATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: bisphosphonate taken weekly with a full glass of water, staying upright
ALENDRONATE.rationale: This drug can cause esophagitis. Separate it from food, calcium, and other drugs by at least 30 minutes.

RISEDRONATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral bisphosphonate for osteoporosis with the same upright dosing rules
RISEDRONATE.rationale: This drug inhibits osteoclasts. Dental exams matter because of rare osteonecrosis of the jaw.

ZOLEDRONIC.clue: Mechanism and effect: yearly IV bisphosphonate that requires adequate hydration and a normal calcium
ZOLEDRONIC.rationale: This drug acid can cause an acute phase reaction. Check creatinine and calcium before each dose.

DENOSUMAB.clue: Mechanism and effect: rANKL inhibitor given every six months that can cause hypocalcemia
DENOSUMAB.rationale: This drug is not a bisphosphonate. Stopping it without a follow-on drug can cause rebound fractures.

RALOXIFENE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sERM that reduces vertebral fractures and raises clot risk
RALOXIFENE.rationale: This drug is an estrogen agonist in bone and an antagonist in breast. It can cause hot flashes and VTE.

CALCITONIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: nasal or injectable hormone sometimes used for acute pain of vertebral fracture
CALCITONIN.rationale: This drug has a small fracture benefit. Nasal irritation is a common effect.

CALCIUM.clue: Mechanism and effect: mineral supplement separated from levothyroxine, quinolones, and tetracyclines
CALCIUM.rationale: This drug binds many drugs in the gut. Citrate is the form that does not need stomach acid.

VITAMIND.clue: Mechanism and effect: supplement needed for calcium absorption and often low in osteoporosis
VITAMIND.rationale: Vitamin D deficiency is corrected before judging a calcium or bisphosphonate plan. Toxicity causes hypercalcemia.

FERROUS.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral iron that causes dark stools and constipation and is best on an empty stomach
FERROUS.rationale: This drug sulfate absorption falls with food, antacids, and tea. Vitamin C juice can help absorption.

FOLICACID.clue: Mechanism and effect: vitamin given before conception and with methotrexate rescue plans in some protocols
FOLICACID.rationale: Folic acid prevents neural tube defects. In methotrexate therapy, folate timing follows the protocol so efficacy is preserved.

PYRIDOXINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: vitamin B6 given with isoniazid to prevent neuropathy
PYRIDOXINE.rationale: This drug is also used for isoniazid overdose seizures. Routine high doses can themselves cause neuropathy.

THIAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: vitamin given before glucose in malnourished patients to prevent Wernicke injury
THIAMINE.rationale: This drug deficiency causes confusion, ataxia, and eye-movement palsy. Replace it in alcohol withdrawal protocols.

POTASSIUM.clue: Mechanism and effect: electrolyte replacement never given as an IV push
POTASSIUM.rationale: Oral This drug is preferred when the gut works. IV This drug is diluted and infused slowly.

MAGNESIUM.clue: Mechanism and effect: electrolyte replaced when potassium will not stay corrected, and the antidote for torsades
MAGNESIUM.rationale: Hypomagnesemia causes refractory hypokalemia. IV This drug treats torsades de pointes.

PHOSPHATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: electrolyte that falls in refeeding and binds oral calcium
PHOSPHATE.rationale: This drug replacement is oral when possible. IV This drug can cause hypocalcemia if given too fast.

SEVELAMER.clue: Mechanism and effect: non-calcium phosphate binder taken with meals in chronic kidney disease
SEVELAMER.rationale: This drug binds dietary phosphate. It does not add to the calcium load the way calcium binders do.

KAYEXALATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sodium polystyrene resin that removes potassium slowly through the gut
KAYEXALATE.rationale: This resin is not the emergency treatment for ECG changes from hyperkalemia. It can cause intestinal injury.

PATIROMER.clue: Mechanism and effect: potassium binder taken with food and separated from other oral drugs
PATIROMER.rationale: This drug exchanges calcium for potassium in the gut. Separate other medications by several hours.

EPOETIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: erythropoiesis-stimulating agent that raises clot and blood pressure risk if hemoglobin is pushed high
EPOETIN.rationale: This drug is used for anemia of chronic kidney disease. Target hemoglobin is not normalized.

AMOXICILLIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: aminopenicillin for otitis, sinusitis, and strep throat
AMOXICILLIN.rationale: This drug is a beta-lactam. A rash during mono is common and is not always a true allergy.

AMPICILLIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: aminopenicillin used for enterococcal infection and some meningitis regimens
AMPICILLIN.rationale: This drug covers susceptible enterococci. A high IV dose is used when meningitis coverage is intended.

PENICILLIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: beta-lactam of choice for syphilis and many streptococcal infections
PENICILLIN.rationale: This drug G remains the treatment for syphilis. Allergy history decides whether a cephalosporin is reasonable.

NAFCILLIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: antistaphylococcal penicillin cleared by the liver, used for serious MSSA
NAFCILLIN.rationale: This drug does not need renal adjustment. It can cause interstitial nephritis.

OXACILLIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: penicillinase-resistant penicillin for methicillin-sensitive staph
OXACILLIN.rationale: This drug is used for MSSA. It does not cover MRSA or enterococci.

CEFAZOLIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: first-generation cephalosporin used for surgical prophylaxis
CEFAZOLIN.rationale: This drug covers skin flora including MSSA. It is the usual pre-incision antibiotic.

CEPHALEXIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral first-generation cephalosporin for skin and urinary infections
CEPHALEXIN.rationale: This drug is taken several times a day. It does not cover MRSA.

CEFTRIAXONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: third-generation cephalosporin for meningitis, gonorrhea, and serious gram-negative infection
CEFTRIAXONE.rationale: This drug reaches the CSF. It can sludge the gallbladder and is avoided with calcium-containing IV fluids in neonates.

CEFEPIME.clue: Mechanism and effect: fourth-generation cephalosporin with pseudomonas coverage
CEFEPIME.rationale: This drug can cause neurotoxicity when the dose is not reduced for kidney function.

CEFTAZIDIME.clue: Mechanism and effect: third-generation cephalosporin used when pseudomonas coverage is needed
CEFTAZIDIME.rationale: This drug lacks reliable gram-positive coverage. It is a pseudomonas cephalosporin.

MEROPENEM.clue: Mechanism and effect: carbapenem for resistant infection that can lower the seizure threshold
MEROPENEM.rationale: This drug covers anaerobes and many resistant gram-negatives. Dose is reduced in renal failure.

IMIPENEM.clue: Mechanism and effect: carbapenem given with cilastatin and known for seizure risk
IMIPENEM.rationale: This drug is paired with cilastatin to block renal breakdown. Seizure risk is higher than with meropenem.

ERTAPENEM.clue: Mechanism and effect: once-daily carbapenem that does not cover pseudomonas or acinetobacter
ERTAPENEM.rationale: This drug is convenient but is the wrong carbapenem when pseudomonas is a concern.

AZTREONAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: monobactam safe in most penicillin allergies, covering aerobic gram-negatives
AZTREONAM.rationale: This drug has no gram-positive or anaerobic activity. It can be used when a beta-lactam allergy is severe.

VANCOMYCIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: glycopeptide for MRSA that is infused slowly to avoid flushing
VANCOMYCIN.rationale: This drug flushing is rate related. Trough or AUC monitoring limits kidney injury.

DAPTOMYCIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: lipopeptide for resistant gram-positive infection that is inactivated by lung surfactant
DAPTOMYCIN.rationale: This drug is not used for pneumonia. It can raise CPK, so muscle symptoms are reported.

LINEZOLID.clue: Mechanism and effect: oxazolidinone for MRSA and VRE that can cause serotonin syndrome
LINEZOLID.rationale: This drug is a weak MAO inhibitor. Thrombocytopenia rises with courses longer than two weeks.

GENTAMICIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: aminoglycoside monitored for kidney and ear toxicity with peaks and troughs
GENTAMICIN.rationale: This drug is often once daily for synergy or traditional dosing. Troughs that stay high predict toxicity.

TOBRAMYCIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: aminoglycoside often chosen for pseudomonas, with the same toxicity profile
TOBRAMYCIN.rationale: This drug needs renal dosing and hearing checks on long courses. It is given with a cell-wall agent for synergy.

AMIKACIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: aminoglycoside reserved for more resistant gram-negative organisms
AMIKACIN.rationale: This drug is dosed by kidney function. It shares ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity with the class.

DOXYCYCLINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: tetracycline for Lyme disease, acne, and atypical pneumonia that stains teeth
DOXYCYCLINE.rationale: This drug is avoided in pregnancy and young children. Separate it from iron, calcium, and antacids.

MINOCYCLINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: tetracycline used for acne that can cause vestibular symptoms and blue-gray skin
MINOCYCLINE.rationale: This drug is separated from divalent cations. Drug-induced lupus is a rare effect.

CLINDAMYCIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: lincosamide with anaerobic coverage and a high risk of C. difficile
CLINDAMYCIN.rationale: This drug diarrhea is assumed to be C. difficile until proven otherwise. It also covers some MRSA skin infection.

TINIDAZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: nitroimidazole for trichomonas, giardia, and some anaerobic infections
TINIDAZOLE.rationale: This drug has a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol, similar to metronidazole.

FOSFOMYCIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: single-dose oral antibiotic for uncomplicated cystitis
FOSFOMYCIN.rationale: This drug is mixed in water and taken once. It is not the drug for pyelonephritis.

FLUCONAZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: azole antifungal for candida that inhibits CYP enzymes
FLUCONAZOLE.rationale: This drug raises levels of warfarin, some statins, and phenytoin. A one-time dose treats uncomplicated vaginal candida.

CASPOFUNGIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: echinocandin for invasive candida that is not absorbed orally
CASPOFUNGIN.rationale: This drug is IV only. It is preferred for unstable candidemia over fluconazole.

MICAFUNGIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: echinocandin alternative for candidemia with few drug interactions
MICAFUNGIN.rationale: This drug covers candida species including many fluconazole-resistant isolates. It does not treat cryptococcus.

NYSTATIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: topical or swish antifungal for thrush that is not systemically absorbed
NYSTATIN.rationale: This drug suspension is swished and swallowed. It will not treat invasive fungal disease.

TERBINAFINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral antifungal for nail dermatophyte infection that can injure the liver
TERBINAFINE.rationale: This drug is taken for weeks for onychomycosis. Check the liver and watch for taste change.

ACYCLOVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiviral for herpes that needs hydration to protect the kidneys
ACYCLOVIR.rationale: This drug crystals can obstruct tubules. Oral doses are adjusted for creatinine clearance.

GANCICLOVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiviral for cytomegalovirus that causes bone marrow suppression
GANCICLOVIR.rationale: This drug is handled as a hazardous drug. Neutropenia is the limiting toxicity.

FAMCICLOVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral prodrug of penciclovir used for herpes zoster and recurrent genital herpes
FAMCICLOVIR.rationale: This drug is started early in a zoster outbreak. Dose is reduced in kidney disease.

OSELTAMIVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: neuraminidase inhibitor most useful within 48 hours of influenza onset
OSELTAMIVIR.rationale: This drug shortens flu illness. Neuropsychiatric effects are reported, and the dose is renal.

ZANAMIVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: inhaled neuraminidase inhibitor avoided in asthma and COPD
ZANAMIVIR.rationale: This drug can cause bronchospasm. It is not the flu drug for a patient who cannot inhale a powder.

BALOXAVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: single-dose endonuclease inhibitor for influenza
BALOXAVIR.rationale: This drug is one dose. It is not combined casually with polyvalent cations, which bind it.

RIBAVIRIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiviral used in some hepatitis C regimens that is teratogenic
RIBAVIRIN.rationale: This drug requires two forms of contraception during and after therapy because of birth defects.

SOFOSBUVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: nS5B inhibitor used in hepatitis C combinations
SOFOSBUVIR.rationale: This drug is the backbone of several hepatitis C regimens. Amiodarone with it can cause severe bradycardia.

TENOFOVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: nucleotide analog for HIV and hepatitis B that can injure kidneys and bone
TENOFOVIR.rationale: This drug disoproxil is the salt linked with Fanconi syndrome. The alafenamide salt has less kidney and bone toxicity.

LAMIVUDINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: cytosine analog for HIV and hepatitis B with a low barrier if used alone for hepatitis B
LAMIVUDINE.rationale: This drug monotherapy for hepatitis B selects resistance. It is well tolerated.

ABACAVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: nucleoside analog that requires HLA-B5701 screening because of hypersensitivity
ABACAVIR.rationale: Never rechallenge This drug after a hypersensitivity reaction. The reaction can include fever, rash, and respiratory symptoms.

RALTEGRAVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: integrase inhibitor for HIV with few drug interactions
RALTEGRAVIR.rationale: This drug can raise CPK. It is taken with or without food depending on the formulation.

EFAVIRENZ.clue: Mechanism and effect: nNRTI that causes vivid dreams and is taken on an empty stomach at bedtime
EFAVIRENZ.rationale: This drug is teratogenic in animal data and is CNS active. Food increases levels and side effects.

RITONAVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: strong CYP3A4 inhibitor used as a pharmacokinetic booster
RITONAVIR.rationale: This drug raises levels of many drugs. Review the whole medication list before it is added.

COBICISTAT.clue: Mechanism and effect: pharmacokinetic booster that inhibits CYP3A4 and raises creatinine slightly
COBICISTAT.rationale: This drug blocks tubular creatinine secretion, so the creatinine bump is not always a GFR drop.

ATAZANAVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: protease inhibitor that needs an acid stomach and can cause jaundice
ATAZANAVIR.rationale: This drug is not combined with proton pump inhibitors in treatment-experienced patients. Indirect bilirubin rises.

DARUNAVIR.clue: Mechanism and effect: protease inhibitor boosted with ritonavir or cobicistat and used with a sulfa caution
DARUNAVIR.rationale: This drug contains a sulfa moiety. Rash is possible in sulfa-allergic patients, and it is taken with food.

ISONIAZID.clue: Mechanism and effect: tuberculosis drug that causes neuropathy unless pyridoxine is given
ISONIAZID.rationale: This drug is hepatotoxic and depletes vitamin B6. A positive hepatitis symptom means stop and check enzymes.

RIFAMPIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: potent CYP inducer used for tuberculosis that turns body fluids orange
RIFAMPIN.rationale: This drug lowers levels of warfarin, oral contraceptives, and many antiretrovirals. Counsel about orange urine.

RIFABUTIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: rifamycin with fewer CYP interactions, used when rifampin cannot be combined
RIFABUTIN.rationale: This drug still induces enzymes, but less than rifampin. Uveitis is a toxicity.

ETHAMBUTOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: tuberculosis drug that can cause optic neuritis
ETHAMBUTOL.rationale: This drug toxicity is color-vision loss. Baseline and periodic eye exams are part of safe use.

BEDAQUILINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: drug for resistant tuberculosis that prolongs the QT interval
BEDAQUILINE.rationale: This drug is used in multidrug-resistant tuberculosis regimens. ECG monitoring is required.

DAPSONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: drug for leprosy and pneumocystis prevention that causes hemolysis in G6PD deficiency
DAPSONE.rationale: This drug is oxidant stress. Screen for G6PD deficiency before use when possible.

ATOVAQUONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: drug for pneumocystis and with proguanil for malaria, taken with food
ATOVAQUONE.rationale: This drug absorption needs dietary fat. It is an option when trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole cannot be used.

PRIMAQUINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antimalarial that eradicates liver stages and causes hemolysis in G6PD deficiency
PRIMAQUINE.rationale: This drug is the hypnozoite drug for vivax and ovale. Test G6PD before the first dose.

CHLOROQUINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antimalarial that can cause retinal toxicity with long use
CHLOROQUINE.rationale: This drug is also used in some autoimmune disease. Eye exams are required for chronic therapy.

QUININE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antimalarial that causes cinchonism: tinnitus, headache, and visual change
QUININE.rationale: This drug is not a casual leg-cramp drug. It prolongs the QT and causes hypoglycemia.

ARTESUNATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: iV artemisinin used for severe malaria
ARTESUNATE.rationale: This drug is the preferred parenteral treatment for severe malaria. Delayed hemolysis can follow treatment.

ALBENDAZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: anthelmintic taken with a fatty meal for tissue parasites
ALBENDAZOLE.rationale: This drug is used for neurocysticercosis and some worm infections. Liver enzymes are checked on long courses.

IVERMECTIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiparasitic for strongyloides and onchocerciasis, taken on an empty stomach
IVERMECTIN.rationale: This drug does not kill adult onchocerca immediately. Mazzotti reactions can follow treatment of onchocerciasis.

PERMETHRIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: topical scabicide applied from neck to toes and washed off after the labeled time
PERMETHRIN.rationale: This drug 5 percent is the usual scabies treatment. Household contacts are treated at the same time.

SERTRALINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sSRI with fewer CYP interactions than fluoxetine or paroxetine
SERTRALINE.rationale: This drug takes weeks for mood. Combining it with MAO inhibitors or linezolid risks serotonin syndrome.

FLUOXETINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: long half-life SSRI that inhibits CYP2D6
FLUOXETINE.rationale: This drug and its metabolite linger for weeks. A long washout is needed before an MAO inhibitor.

PAROXETINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sSRI most associated with withdrawal symptoms and CYP2D6 inhibition
PAROXETINE.rationale: This drug is more anticholinergic than other SSRIs and is avoided in pregnancy when possible.

CITALOPRAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: sSRI with a dose cap because of QT prolongation
CITALOPRAM.rationale: This drug doses above 40 mg are avoided, and above 20 mg in older adults, because of the QT risk.

VENLAFAXINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sNRI that can raise blood pressure as the dose increases
VENLAFAXINE.rationale: This drug withdrawal is uncomfortable if it is stopped suddenly. Check blood pressure at higher doses.

DULOXETINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sNRI used for depression and neuropathic or musculoskeletal pain
DULOXETINE.rationale: This drug is avoided in substantial liver disease and in severe kidney disease. It can raise blood pressure.

BUPROPION.clue: Mechanism and effect: antidepressant that lowers the seizure threshold and helps with smoking cessation
BUPROPION.rationale: This drug is avoided in bulimia, anorexia, and seizure disorders. It does not cause SSRI sexual side effects.

MIRTAZAPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antidepressant that causes sedation and increased appetite
MIRTAZAPINE.rationale: This drug is useful when insomnia and poor appetite are problems. Weight gain is expected.

TRAZODONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: sedating antidepressant used for sleep that can cause priapism
TRAZODONE.rationale: This drug is not a benzodiazepine. A prolonged erection is an emergency.

DOXEPIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: tricyclic used in low doses for sleep and itching, with anticholinergic effects at higher doses
DOXEPIN.rationale: This drug in depression doses prolongs the QT and is dangerous in overdose. Low doses are for insomnia.

IMIPRAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: tricyclic antidepressant with anticholinergic effects and cardiac toxicity in overdose
IMIPRAMINE.rationale: This drug overdose causes seizures and wide-complex arrhythmias. It is not a first-line antidepressant.

PHENELZINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: irreversible MAO inhibitor that requires a low-tyramine diet
PHENELZINE.rationale: This drug plus an SSRI, meperidine, or dextromethorphan can cause serotonin syndrome or a hypertensive crisis.

SELEGILINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: mAO-B inhibitor for Parkinson disease; the patch can lose selectivity
SELEGILINE.rationale: Dietary tyramine restrictions apply to higher-dose This drug patch, not always to low oral MAO-B doses.

HALOPERIDOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: first-generation antipsychotic that causes dystonia and QT prolongation
HALOPERIDOL.rationale: This drug is not used IV without caution because of the QT. Acute dystonia is treated with an anticholinergic.

RISPERIDONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: atypical antipsychotic with a relatively high risk of prolactin elevation and EPS
RISPERIDONE.rationale: This drug causes hyperprolactinemia. Dose-related extrapyramidal symptoms are more common than with quetiapine.

OLANZAPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: atypical antipsychotic with marked weight gain and metabolic effects
OLANZAPINE.rationale: This drug is sedating and anticholinergic. Smoking induces its clearance.

QUETIAPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: atypical antipsychotic often used for sedation, with metabolic risk and a low EPS risk
QUETIAPINE.rationale: This drug is sometimes misused for sleep. It still causes weight gain and QT effects.

ZIPRASIDONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: atypical antipsychotic that must be taken with food and prolongs the QT
ZIPRASIDONE.rationale: This drug absorption doubles with a meal of adequate calories. It is avoided when the QT is already long.

LURASIDONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: atypical antipsychotic taken with food that has less metabolic effect than olanzapine
LURASIDONE.rationale: This drug is taken with at least 350 calories. It is a CYP3A4 substrate.

CLOZAPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: most effective antipsychotic, reserved for treatment resistance because of agranulocytosis
CLOZAPINE.rationale: This drug requires absolute neutrophil count monitoring. Constipation, sialorrhea, and myocarditis are other risks.

LITHIUM.clue: Mechanism and effect: mood stabilizer with a narrow therapeutic index that rises when sodium is lost
LITHIUM.rationale: This drug toxicity follows dehydration, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, and thiazides. Tremor and confusion are early signs.

VALPROATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: mood stabilizer and antiseizure drug that is teratogenic and hepatotoxic
VALPROATE.rationale: This drug is avoided in pregnancy. Ammonia is checked if cognition changes, and platelets can fall.

LAMOTRIGINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiseizure and mood drug titrated slowly because of Stevens-Johnson risk
LAMOTRIGINE.rationale: Valproate doubles This drug levels, so the titration is slower. Any rash stops the drug.

LORAZEPAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: benzodiazepine preferred in liver disease because it is glucuronidated
LORAZEPAM.rationale: This drug is used for status epilepticus and alcohol withdrawal. It depresses breathing with opioids.

DIAZEPAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting benzodiazepine for seizures, spasms, and alcohol withdrawal
DIAZEPAM.rationale: This drug has active metabolites. It accumulates in older adults and in liver disease.

ALPRAZOLAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: short-acting benzodiazepine with a difficult withdrawal
ALPRAZOLAM.rationale: This drug is tapered. Abrupt cessation can cause rebound anxiety and seizures.

CLONAZEPAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting benzodiazepine used for panic and some seizure types
CLONAZEPAM.rationale: This drug lasts longer than alprazolam. Sedation and dependence are the counseling points.

MIDAZOLAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: short-acting benzodiazepine used for procedural sedation
MIDAZOLAM.rationale: This drug is reversed with flumazenil only when the airway is protected and chronic use is unlikely.

FLUMAZENIL.clue: Mechanism and effect: benzodiazepine antagonist that can precipitate seizures
FLUMAZENIL.rationale: This drug is avoided in chronic benzodiazepine use and in mixed overdoses with proconvulsant drugs.

ZOLPIDEM.clue: Mechanism and effect: non-benzodiazepine hypnotic with complex sleep behaviors
ZOLPIDEM.rationale: This drug is taken only when ready for bed. Lower doses are used in women and older adults.

ESZOPICLONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: hypnotic that can leave a metallic taste
ESZOPICLONE.rationale: This drug is a controlled sleep drug. Next-day impairment is possible.

BUSPIRONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: non-sedating anxiolytic that takes weeks and has no cross-tolerance with benzodiazepines
BUSPIRONE.rationale: This drug is not a rescue drug for a panic attack. It is a scheduled anxiolytic.

AMPHETAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: stimulant for ADHD that raises heart rate and blood pressure and suppresses appetite
AMPHETAMINE.rationale: Amphetamines are controlled substances. They are avoided in structural heart disease and uncontrolled hypertension.

ATOMOXETINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: non-stimulant ADHD drug that is a CYP2D6 substrate and carries a suicidal-ideation warning
ATOMOXETINE.rationale: This drug takes weeks. It can raise blood pressure and is not a controlled stimulant.

GUANFACINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: alpha-2 agonist for ADHD that is not stopped abruptly
GUANFACINE.rationale: This drug extended release can cause hypotension and rebound hypertension if stopped suddenly.

CLONIDINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: central alpha agonist whose sudden stop causes rebound hypertension
CLONIDINE.rationale: This drug patches are replaced on schedule. The oral drug is tapered.

DONEPEZIL.clue: Mechanism and effect: cholinesterase inhibitor for Alzheimer disease that causes GI upset and bradycardia
DONEPEZIL.rationale: This drug increases acetylcholine. Diarrhea, vivid dreams, and a slow heart rate are expected effects.

GALANTAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: cholinesterase inhibitor taken with food that needs renal and hepatic dose limits
GALANTAMINE.rationale: This drug shares the cholinergic side effects of donepezil. Dose is reduced when clearance is low.

MEMANTINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: nMDA antagonist for moderate Alzheimer disease that is renally dosed
MEMANTINE.rationale: This drug is often added to a cholinesterase inhibitor. Dizziness and confusion can occur.

CARBIDOPA.clue: Mechanism and effect: decarboxylase inhibitor that lets more levodopa reach the brain
CARBIDOPA.rationale: This drug reduces peripheral nausea from levodopa. It does not treat Parkinson disease by itself.

LEVODOPA.clue: Mechanism and effect: dopamine precursor for Parkinson disease that causes dyskinesias over time
LEVODOPA.rationale: This drug is the most effective motor drug. Protein meals can compete with its absorption.

ENTACAPONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: cOMT inhibitor that extends levodopa effect and can darken urine
ENTACAPONE.rationale: This drug is only useful with levodopa. Diarrhea and brown-orange urine are counseling points.

PRAMIPEXOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: dopamine agonist that can cause sudden sleep and impulse-control problems
PRAMIPEXOLE.rationale: This drug is renally cleared. Warn about gambling, hypersexuality, and falling asleep while driving.

ROPINIROLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: dopamine agonist also used for restless legs
ROPINIROLE.rationale: This drug is metabolized by CYP1A2. Smoking changes its levels, and impulse-control disorders occur.

BENZTROPINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: anticholinergic for drug-induced parkinsonism and dystonia
BENZTROPINE.rationale: This drug is avoided in older adults because of confusion, retention, and constipation.

MORPHINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: full opioid agonist that releases histamine and is renally cleared to an active metabolite
MORPHINE.rationale: This drug causes constipation, which is prevented, not waited for. Active metabolites accumulate in kidney failure.

OXYCODONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral opioid available alone or with acetaminophen
OXYCODONE.rationale: This drug combination products hide acetaminophen. Total daily acetaminophen must stay within the limit.

HYDROCODONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: opioid usually combined with acetaminophen for short-term pain
HYDROCODONE.rationale: This drug products are controlled. Counsel on constipation, sedation, and the acetaminophen ceiling.

FENTANYL.clue: Mechanism and effect: potent opioid patch that is not for opioid-naive acute pain
FENTANYL.rationale: This drug patches take about a day to reach effect and linger after removal. Heat increases absorption.

METHADONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting opioid for pain and opioid use disorder that prolongs the QT
METHADONE.rationale: This drug accumulates for days. Dose changes are made slowly, and interacting drugs raise the QT risk.

NALOXONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: opioid antagonist used for overdose, with a shorter duration than many opioids
NALOXONE.rationale: This drug is repeated because respiratory depression can return. It precipitates withdrawal.

NALTREXONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral or monthly opioid antagonist for alcohol or opioid use disorder
NALTREXONE.rationale: This drug is not started until opioids have cleared, or it will precipitate withdrawal. It is hepatotoxic at high doses.

TRAMADOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: weak opioid that also raises serotonin and lowers the seizure threshold
TRAMADOL.rationale: This drug plus an SSRI risks serotonin syndrome. Seizure risk rises with high doses and interacting drugs.

MEPERIDINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: opioid avoided chronically because the metabolite normeperidine causes seizures
MEPERIDINE.rationale: This drug with an MAO inhibitor is contraindicated. It is not a preferred pain drug.

CODEINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: prodrug of morphine that is dangerous in ultra-rapid CYP2D6 metabolizers
CODEINE.rationale: This drug is avoided in children after tonsillectomy. Breastfeeding ultra-rapid metabolizers can overdose an infant.

IBUPROFEN.clue: Mechanism and effect: nSAID that can worsen heart failure, kidneys, and ulcers
IBUPROFEN.rationale: This drug blocks COX. It raises blood pressure and blunts the effect of some antihypertensives.

NAPROXEN.clue: Mechanism and effect: longer-acting NSAID with the same renal and gastrointestinal risks
NAPROXEN.rationale: This drug is taken with food. It is avoided in the third trimester because of ductus closure.

KETOROLAC.clue: Mechanism and effect: potent NSAID limited to a few days because of bleeding and kidney injury
KETOROLAC.rationale: This drug is not for chronic pain. The total course, IV plus oral, stays short.

CELECOXIB.clue: Mechanism and effect: cOX-2 inhibitor with less ulcer risk than nonselective NSAIDs but the same heart caution
CELECOXIB.rationale: This drug is a sulfonamide. Cardiovascular risk still applies, and it is not used in significant heart failure.

DICLOFENAC.clue: Mechanism and effect: nSAID available oral and topical, with notable cardiovascular risk
DICLOFENAC.rationale: Topical This drug still has some systemic absorption. Oral This drug is among the higher cardiovascular-risk NSAIDs.

MELOXICAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: once-daily NSAID that is somewhat COX-2 preferring at low doses
MELOXICAM.rationale: This drug is easier to adhere to than ibuprofen. Renal and ulcer warnings remain.

GABAPENTIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: anticonvulsant for neuropathic pain that is renally cleared and sedating
GABAPENTIN.rationale: This drug is titrated. Misuse and respiratory depression with opioids are current warnings.

PREGABALIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: gabapentinoid for neuropathic pain and fibromyalgia that causes edema and dizziness
PREGABALIN.rationale: This drug is a controlled substance. Dose is reduced when creatinine clearance falls.

BACLOFEN.clue: Mechanism and effect: gABA-B agonist for spasticity that can cause seizures if stopped suddenly
BACLOFEN.rationale: Intrathecal This drug withdrawal is an emergency. Oral This drug is tapered.

TIZANIDINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: alpha-2 agonist muscle relaxant that causes hypotension and is affected by CYP1A2 inhibitors
TIZANIDINE.rationale: This drug with ciprofloxacin or fluvoxamine can cause dangerous hypotension. It is hepatotoxic.

SUMATRIPTAN.clue: Mechanism and effect: serotonin agonist for migraine that is contraindicated in coronary disease
SUMATRIPTAN.rationale: This drug is not used within 24 hours of an ergot. Chest pressure can occur even without ischemia.

RIZATRIPTAN.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral triptan whose dose is reduced when propranolol is taken
RIZATRIPTAN.rationale: Propranolol raises This drug levels. The migraine dose is lowered in that combination.

ERGOTAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: ergot for migraine that causes severe vasoconstriction with CYP3A4 inhibitors
ERGOTAMINE.rationale: This drug is contraindicated with macrolides and protease inhibitors. It is also contraindicated in pregnancy.

TOPIRAMATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiseizure drug used for migraine prevention that causes cognitive slowing and kidney stones
TOPIRAMATE.rationale: This drug is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor. It reduces the effectiveness of estrogen contraceptives at higher doses.

OMEPRAZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: proton pump inhibitor taken before breakfast for ulcer and reflux
OMEPRAZOLE.rationale: This drug can lower magnesium and B12 over time and raises C. difficile risk. It inhibits clopidogrel activation.

RABEPRAZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: proton pump inhibitor with less CYP2C19 dependence than omeprazole
RABEPRAZOLE.rationale: This drug is an acid-suppression option when a CYP2C19 interaction is a concern.

FAMOTIDINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: h2 blocker adjusted for kidney function
FAMOTIDINE.rationale: This drug does not inhibit CYP enzymes the way cimetidine does. Confusion can occur when the dose is too high for the kidneys.

CIMETIDINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: h2 blocker that inhibits many CYP enzymes and causes antiandrogen effects
CIMETIDINE.rationale: This drug raises levels of warfarin, phenytoin, and other drugs. It is rarely a first H2 blocker now.

SUCRALFATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: ulcer coating agent given on an empty stomach that binds other drugs
SUCRALFATE.rationale: This drug needs acid to work, so it is not paired with continuous acid suppression. Separate interacting drugs.

MISOPROSTOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: prostaglandin that prevents NSAID ulcers and is contraindicated in pregnancy
MISOPROSTOL.rationale: This drug causes uterine contraction. Diarrhea is the limiting side effect.

BISMUTH.clue: Mechanism and effect: agent in some ulcer and diarrhea regimens that blackens the stool and tongue
BISMUTH.rationale: This drug subsalicylate contains salicylate. It is avoided in children with viral illness and in salicylate allergy.

ONDANSETRON.clue: Mechanism and effect: 5-HT3 antiemetic that prolongs the QT interval
ONDANSETRON.rationale: This drug is used for chemotherapy and postoperative nausea. It is not the drug for motion sickness.

GRANISETRON.clue: Mechanism and effect: 5-HT3 antagonist available as a patch for chemotherapy nausea
GRANISETRON.rationale: This drug shares the QT warning of the class. The patch is applied before chemotherapy.

APREPITANT.clue: Mechanism and effect: nK1 antagonist for delayed chemotherapy nausea that interacts with CYP3A4
APREPITANT.rationale: This drug can change the dose needs of dexamethasone and hormonal contraceptives.

DOMPERIDONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: peripheral dopamine antagonist for nausea that prolongs the QT
DOMPERIDONE.rationale: This drug does not cross the blood-brain barrier well, so it causes less central dystonia than metoclopramide.

LOPERAMIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: opioid antidiarrheal that does not cross the blood-brain barrier at usual doses
LOPERAMIDE.rationale: High-dose This drug abuse causes cardiac arrhythmias. It is not used when fever or bloody stool suggests invasive diarrhea.

DOCUSATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: stool softener that does not stimulate the colon
DOCUSATE.rationale: This drug is for prevention of straining. It will not empty a constipated colon by itself.

SENNA.clue: Mechanism and effect: stimulant laxative used short term or with opioids
SENNA.rationale: This drug causes cramping. Melanosis coli can follow long use and is a marker of chronic stimulant laxatives.

BISACODYL.clue: Mechanism and effect: stimulant laxative tablet that should not be crushed or taken with antacids
BISACODYL.rationale: Enteric This drug dissolves in the colon. Antacids can cause it to release early and irritate the stomach.

LACTULOSE.clue: Mechanism and effect: osmotic laxative that also lowers ammonia in hepatic encephalopathy
LACTULOSE.rationale: This drug is titrated to a few soft stools a day in encephalopathy. Too much causes dehydration.

PSYLLIUM.clue: Mechanism and effect: bulk fiber laxative taken with a full glass of water
PSYLLIUM.rationale: This drug without enough fluid can swell and obstruct. Separate it from other oral drugs.

MESALAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: 5-ASA drug for ulcerative colitis, released at different gut sites by formulation
MESALAMINE.rationale: This drug formulations are not interchangeable. Nephrotoxicity is rare but creatinine is checked.

BUDESONIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: steroid with high first-pass metabolism used for some inflammatory bowel disease
BUDESONIDE.rationale: Oral This drug acts in the gut with less systemic steroid effect than prednisone, but not zero.

INFLIXIMAB.clue: Mechanism and effect: iV TNF inhibitor that can reactivate tuberculosis
INFLIXIMAB.rationale: This drug requires tuberculosis and hepatitis B screening. Infusion reactions are treated and sometimes premedicated.

ADALIMUMAB.clue: Mechanism and effect: subcutaneous TNF inhibitor with the same infection warnings as infliximab
ADALIMUMAB.rationale: This drug is injected at home. Live vaccines are avoided during therapy.

OCTREOTIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: somatostatin analog for variceal bleeding and some secretory tumors
OCTREOTIDE.rationale: This drug reduces splanchnic blood flow. It is used with endoscopy, not instead of it, for varices.

URSODIOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: bile acid used to dissolve some gallstones and to treat primary biliary cholangitis
URSODIOL.rationale: This drug is taken with food. It does not dissolve calcified or pigment stones well.

ALBUTEROL.clue: Mechanism and effect: short-acting beta agonist rescue inhaler that causes tremor and tachycardia
ALBUTEROL.rationale: This drug is not a controller. Rising use means the preventive inhaler needs review.

SALMETEROL.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting beta agonist that is never used alone in asthma
SALMETEROL.rationale: This drug without an inhaled corticosteroid increases asthma death risk. It is paired with a steroid.

FORMOTEROL.clue: Mechanism and effect: fast-onset long-acting beta agonist used with an inhaled corticosteroid
FORMOTEROL.rationale: This drug can be part of a maintenance-and-reliever regimen. It is not a standalone asthma drug.

TIOTROPIUM.clue: Mechanism and effect: long-acting antimuscarinic inhaler for COPD
TIOTROPIUM.rationale: This drug dries secretions and can cause urinary retention. It is inhaled, not swallowed.

IPRATROPIUM.clue: Mechanism and effect: short-acting antimuscarinic used with albuterol in COPD exacerbations
IPRATROPIUM.rationale: This drug is a reliever. Closed-angle glaucoma can worsen if the mist gets in the eyes.

FLUTICASONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: inhaled corticosteroid that can cause thrush and hoarseness
FLUTICASONE.rationale: Patients rinse and spit after This drug. High doses have some systemic steroid effect.

MOMETASONE.clue: Mechanism and effect: inhaled or nasal corticosteroid for asthma or allergic rhinitis
MOMETASONE.rationale: This drug is a controller or a nasal steroid, not a rescue inhaler.

MONTELUKAST.clue: Mechanism and effect: leukotriene blocker for asthma and allergic rhinitis with a neuropsychiatric warning
MONTELUKAST.rationale: This drug is taken in the evening for asthma. Mood and sleep changes are reported.

ZAFIRLUKAST.clue: Mechanism and effect: leukotriene receptor antagonist taken on an empty stomach
ZAFIRLUKAST.rationale: This drug food reduces absorption. Hepatotoxicity is monitored.

ZILEUTON.clue: Mechanism and effect: 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor for asthma that requires liver monitoring
ZILEUTON.rationale: This drug inhibits theophylline metabolism. ALT is checked.

OMALIZUMAB.clue: Mechanism and effect: anti-IgE injection for allergic asthma given in a setting that can treat anaphylaxis
OMALIZUMAB.rationale: This drug dose depends on weight and IgE level. Patients are observed after injection.

ROFLUMILAST.clue: Mechanism and effect: pDE-4 inhibitor for severe COPD that causes weight loss and psychiatric effects
ROFLUMILAST.rationale: This drug is not a bronchodilator. Diarrhea and weight loss limit its use.

DORNASE.clue: Mechanism and effect: inhaled enzyme that cleaves DNA in cystic fibrosis sputum
DORNASE.rationale: This drug alfa is not mixed with other nebulized drugs in the same cup. It thins infected secretions.

GUAIFENESIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: expectorant taken with water to loosen mucus
GUAIFENESIN.rationale: This drug does not suppress cough. Hydration is part of how it is used.

BENZONATATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: prescription cough capsule that must be swallowed whole
BENZONATATE.rationale: Chewing This drug can numb the mouth and cause choking. It is dangerous in children.

ALLOPURINOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: xanthine oxidase inhibitor for gout prevention, not the treatment of an acute flare alone
ALLOPURINOL.rationale: This drug is titrated to the uric acid goal. A rash can be severe, especially with certain HLA types.

FEBUXOSTAT.clue: Mechanism and effect: xanthine oxidase inhibitor reserved when allopurinol cannot be used
FEBUXOSTAT.rationale: This drug carries a cardiovascular warning. It is still a urate-lowering drug, not an acute-flare drug.

PROBENECID.clue: Mechanism and effect: uricosuric that is avoided in kidney stones and during an acute flare
PROBENECID.rationale: This drug blocks penicillin excretion and raises beta-lactam levels. It needs adequate urine flow.

COLCHICINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: anti-inflammatory for early gout flares that causes diarrhea
COLCHICINE.rationale: This drug dose is reduced with strong CYP3A4 or P-glycoprotein inhibitors and in kidney disease.

PEGLICASE.clue: Mechanism and effect: iV uricase for refractory gout that can cause infusion reactions
PEGLICASE.rationale: Pegloticase is stopped if uric acid rises, because that signals antibody formation and a higher reaction risk.

LEFLUNOMIDE.clue: Mechanism and effect: dMARD with a very long half-life that is teratogenic
LEFLUNOMIDE.rationale: This drug is washed out with cholestyramine when pregnancy is planned. Liver enzymes are monitored.

TACROLIMUS.clue: Mechanism and effect: calcineurin inhibitor with a narrow index, nephrotoxicity, and CYP3A4 interactions
TACROLIMUS.rationale: This drug levels are troughs. Grapefruit and many antifungals raise the level.

SIROLIMUS.clue: Mechanism and effect: mTOR inhibitor that impairs wound healing and raises lipids
SIROLIMUS.rationale: This drug is not started immediately around major surgery if healing is the priority. Mouth ulcers are common.

FILGRASTIM.clue: Mechanism and effect: g-CSF that raises neutrophils and causes bone pain
FILGRASTIM.rationale: This drug is timed after chemotherapy so it does not stimulate cells still being killed. It is not a chemotherapy drug.

MESNA.clue: Mechanism and effect: uroprotectant given with ifosfamide or high-dose cyclophosphamide
MESNA.rationale: This drug binds acrolein in the bladder. Hemorrhagic cystitis is the toxicity it prevents.

LEUCOVORIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: reduced folate that rescues normal cells after methotrexate
LEUCOVORIN.rationale: This drug timing matters. It is also given to boost fluorouracil in some colorectal regimens.

RASBURICASE.clue: Mechanism and effect: uricase for tumor lysis that is contraindicated in G6PD deficiency
RASBURICASE.rationale: This drug makes uric acid samples fall in the tube. The lab must handle the specimen on ice.

DEXRAZOXANE.clue: Mechanism and effect: chelator that reduces anthracycline heart injury and is also an extravasation antidote
DEXRAZOXANE.rationale: This drug is not routine for every doxorubicin patient. It is used when the cumulative dose is high or for extravasation.

TAMOXIFEN.clue: Mechanism and effect: sERM for estrogen-receptor breast cancer that raises clot and endometrial risk
TAMOXIFEN.rationale: This drug is a prodrug via CYP2D6. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors such as paroxetine can reduce its activation.

ANASTROZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: aromatase inhibitor for postmenopausal hormone-receptor breast cancer
ANASTROZOLE.rationale: This drug causes joint pain and bone loss. It is not the adjuvant endocrine drug for a premenopausal woman alone.

LETROZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: aromatase inhibitor used in postmenopausal breast cancer and some fertility protocols
LETROZOLE.rationale: This drug lowers estrogen. Bone density and cholesterol are followed in long adjuvant use.

IMATINIB.clue: Mechanism and effect: bCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor taken with food and a large glass of water
IMATINIB.rationale: This drug causes edema and muscle cramps. CYP3A4 inducers lower its level.

ERLOTINIB.clue: Mechanism and effect: eGFR inhibitor taken on an empty stomach that causes an acneiform rash
ERLOTINIB.rationale: This drug rash is a class effect. Proton pump inhibitors markedly reduce its absorption.

HYDROXYUREA.clue: Mechanism and effect: ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor for sickle cell disease and some myeloproliferative disease
HYDROXYUREA.rationale: This drug raises fetal hemoglobin in sickle cell disease. Blood counts are followed because it is myelosuppressive.

GRAPEFRUIT.clue: Mechanism and effect: fruit that inhibits intestinal CYP3A4 and raises levels of many drugs
GRAPEFRUIT.rationale: This drug juice is a one-way interaction: it inhibits, it does not induce. The effect can last more than a day.

TYRAMINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: dietary amine that causes hypertensive crisis with MAO inhibitors
TYRAMINE.rationale: Aged cheese, cured meats, and tap beer are high in This drug. Patients on phenelzine need this list.

ALCOHOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: cNS depressant that causes a disulfiram reaction with metronidazole and tinidazole
ALCOHOL.rationale: This drug adds sedation to opioids and benzodiazepines and liver risk to acetaminophen in heavy use.

CHARCOAL.clue: Mechanism and effect: adsorbent used for some recent overdoses that binds other oral drugs
CHARCOAL.rationale: Activated This drug does not bind iron, lithium, or alcohols well. The airway must be protected.

ANTACID.clue: Mechanism and effect: magnesium, aluminum, or calcium product that chelates quinolones and tetracyclines
ANTACID.rationale: Separate antacids from levothyroxine, quinolones, and tetracyclines by several hours.

CHELATION.clue: Mechanism and effect: binding of a drug by calcium, iron, or magnesium that blocks absorption
CHELATION.rationale: This drug is why ciprofloxacin and doxycycline are separated from dairy and supplements.

PRODRUG.clue: Mechanism and effect: inactive compound that must be converted to the active drug
PRODRUG.rationale: Clopidogrel and codeine are prodrugs. Poor metabolizers may get little effect.

FIRSTPASS.clue: Mechanism and effect: liver metabolism of an oral drug before it reaches the circulation
FIRSTPASS.rationale: High first-pass extraction is why some drugs are given IV or as patches. Inhibitors of that path raise levels.

HALFLIFE.clue: Mechanism and effect: time for the plasma concentration to fall by half, used to estimate steady state
HALFLIFE.rationale: About four to five half-lives are needed to reach steady state. A long half-life means a long washout.

CLEARANCE.clue: Mechanism and effect: volume of plasma cleared of drug per unit time
CLEARANCE.rationale: This drug falls in the organ that eliminates the drug. Dose rate is This drug times target concentration.

TROUGH.clue: Mechanism and effect: concentration drawn just before the next dose
TROUGH.rationale: Aminoglycoside and vancomycin troughs, or AUC, are used to limit toxicity.

PEAK.clue: Mechanism and effect: concentration drawn after distribution, reflecting the highest level
PEAK.rationale: Peaks are timed after the infusion ends, not during it. They are used for some aminoglycoside regimens.

BIOEQUIV.clue: Mechanism and effect: standard showing a generic delivers the same exposure as the reference product
BIOEQUIV.rationale: Bioequivalence uses AUC and peak concentration limits. Narrow-therapeutic-index drugs are sometimes debated.

SUBLINGUAL.clue: Mechanism and effect: route that bypasses the gut and first-pass liver metabolism
SUBLINGUAL.rationale: Nitroglycerin tablets are not swallowed. The patient sits, because the blood pressure will fall.

TRANSDERMAL.clue: Mechanism and effect: patch route that gives steady absorption and lingers after removal
TRANSDERMAL.rationale: Fentanyl and clonidine patches are folded and discarded safely. Heat increases absorption.

ENTERIC.clue: Mechanism and effect: coating that keeps a tablet from dissolving in the stomach
ENTERIC.rationale: This drug tablets are not crushed. Bisacodyl and some aspirin products depend on the coating.

INDUCER.clue: Mechanism and effect: drug that increases enzyme activity and lowers substrate levels
INDUCER.rationale: Rifampin, carbamazepine, and phenytoin are classic inducers. The effect takes days to appear and to wear off.

INHIBITOR.clue: Mechanism and effect: drug that blocks an enzyme and raises substrate levels
INHIBITOR.rationale: Azoles, macrolides, and ritonavir inhibit CYP3A4. The interaction can appear with the first doses.

SUBSTRATE.clue: Mechanism and effect: drug that is metabolized by a given enzyme
SUBSTRATE.rationale: A This drug's level rises with an inhibitor and falls with an inducer of its enzyme.

PHENYTOIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: antiseizure drug with nonlinear kinetics and a high protein binding
PHENYTOIN.rationale: This drug small dose changes cause large level changes near the therapeutic range. Low albumin raises the free fraction.

DISULFIRAM.clue: Mechanism and effect: alcohol-deterrent drug that causes flushing and vomiting if ethanol is consumed
DISULFIRAM.rationale: This drug blocks aldehyde dehydrogenase. Hidden alcohol in mouthwash and sauces can trigger the reaction.

NALMEFENE.clue: Mechanism and effect: opioid antagonist related to naloxone with a longer duration in some formulations
NALMEFENE.rationale: Opioid antagonists reverse respiratory depression and can precipitate acute withdrawal.

FOMEPIZOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: alcohol dehydrogenase inhibitor for methanol and ethylene glycol poisoning
FOMEPIZOLE.rationale: This drug blocks formation of toxic metabolites. It is preferred over ethanol when available.

GLUCAGON.clue: Mechanism and effect: hormone used for beta-blocker overdose and for severe hypoglycemia when the patient cannot swallow
GLUCAGON.rationale: This drug raises glucose from liver stores. It will not work well if glycogen is depleted.

SUCCIMER.clue: Mechanism and effect: oral chelator for lead poisoning
SUCCIMER.rationale: This drug is used when the lead level and the clinical picture meet treatment thresholds. It chelates other metals too.

PRALIDOXIME.clue: Mechanism and effect: cholinesterase reactivator given with atropine for organophosphate poisoning
PRALIDOXIME.rationale: This drug works best before the enzyme ages. Atropine treats the muscarinic symptoms.

DIGIFAB.clue: Mechanism and effect: antibody fragments that bind digoxin for life-threatening toxicity
DIGIFAB.rationale: Digoxin immune fab is dosed by the amount ingested or the level. The level after treatment is not interpretable.

SUGAMMADEX.clue: Mechanism and effect: reversal agent that encapsulates rocuronium and vecuronium
SUGAMMADEX.rationale: This drug can bind hormonal contraceptives for a week. It is not a reversal for succinylcholine.

VITAMINK.clue: Mechanism and effect: fat-soluble vitamin that reverses warfarin and must be consistent in the diet
VITAMINK.rationale: Patients do not avoid greens; they keep the intake steady. Pharmaceutical vitamin K is phytonadione.

ORANGEBOOK.clue: Mechanism and effect: fDA reference that rates therapeutic equivalence of generic products
ORANGEBOOK.rationale: An AB rating means the generic is therapeutically equivalent to the reference. Other codes flag unresolved issues.

AUXLABEL.clue: Mechanism and effect: extra sticker that carries a critical counseling point the vial label may not emphasize
AUXLABEL.rationale: Auxiliary labels cover shake well, take with food, and do not crush. They do not replace spoken counseling.

NDCNUMBER.clue: Mechanism and effect: identifier on the package used to pick the correct product at the shelf
NDCNUMBER.rationale: The NDC is not a substitute for reading the drug name and strength. Look-alike packages are a known error source.

TALLMAN.clue: Mechanism and effect: mixed-case lettering that separates look-alike drug names
TALLMAN.rationale: Tall-man letters highlight the dissimilar part of names such as hydrOXYzine and hydrALAZINE.

HIGHALERT.clue: Mechanism and effect: category that includes insulin, opioids, anticoagulants, and concentrated electrolytes
HIGHALERT.rationale: High-alert drugs need independent checks. A tenfold insulin or heparin error is a classic harm.

ISMP.clue: Mechanism and effect: organization that publishes high-alert lists and error-prevention standards
ISMP.rationale: This drug recommendations drive tall-man letters, do-not-crush lists, and standard concentrations.

BEERS.clue: Mechanism and effect: criteria that list drugs to avoid or dose-reduce in older adults
BEERS.rationale: The This drug list flags glyburide, many anticholinergics, and sliding-scale insulin as higher risk in older adults.

ANTICHOLIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: effect that causes dry mouth, constipation, retention, and confusion
ANTICHOLIN.rationale: Anticholinergic burden adds up across drugs. Older adults are especially vulnerable to delirium.

QTPROLONG.clue: Mechanism and effect: effect that raises torsades risk, worsened by low potassium or magnesium
QTPROLONG.rationale: Ondansetron, citalopram, and many antipsychotics prolong the QT. Correct electrolytes and avoid stacking them.

SEROTONIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: syndrome of clonus, hyperreflexia, and agitation from stacked serotonergic drugs
SEROTONIN.rationale: This drug syndrome is neuromuscular hyperactivity. It is not the same as neuroleptic malignant syndrome rigidity.

NARROWTI.clue: Mechanism and effect: therapeutic index small enough that levels or close monitoring are required
NARROWTI.rationale: Narrow therapeutic index drugs include warfarin, lithium, phenytoin, and digoxin.

CREATININE.clue: Mechanism and effect: lab used to estimate kidney function for renal dosing
CREATININE.rationale: This drug clearance equations need a stable This drug, age, weight, and sex. They overestimate function in frail patients.

COCKCROFT.clue: Mechanism and effect: equation that estimates creatinine clearance from age, weight, sex, and creatinine
COCKCROFT.rationale: The This drug-Gault equation is still used in many drug labels. Use actual, ideal, or adjusted weight as the label directs.

IDEALWT.clue: Mechanism and effect: weight based on height and sex, used in some clearance and dose calculations
IDEALWT.rationale: Ideal body weight avoids overdosing renally cleared drugs in patients with obesity when the label says to use it.

BSA.clue: Mechanism and effect: body surface area used to dose many chemotherapy drugs
BSA.rationale: This drug dosing uses height and weight. Recalculate it; do not copy an old value after a large weight change.

MILLIMOLE.clue: Mechanism and effect: unit of amount used for electrolytes such as phosphate and some potassium orders
MILLIMOLE.rationale: Millimoles and milliequivalents are not identical for divalent ions. Read the phosphate order units carefully.

OSMOLARITY.clue: Mechanism and effect: concentration term used to judge whether an IV fluid is isotonic
OSMOLARITY.rationale: Hyperosmolar infusions through a small vein cause phlebitis. Parenteral nutrition This drug limits peripheral use.

ALLIGATION.clue: Mechanism and effect: method for mixing two concentrations to reach a desired strength
ALLIGATION.rationale: This drug solves how many parts of each strength to combine. It does not replace checking the final volume.

DROPS.clue: Mechanism and effect: volume unit for ophthalmic and some oral liquids, which is not exactly a milliliter
DROPS.rationale: A dropper is calibrated to its bottle. Do not substitute a household teaspoon for a measured oral syringe.

INFUSION.clue: Mechanism and effect: intravenous delivery calculated from concentration, rate, and time
INFUSION.rationale: This drug rate errors are prevented by standard concentrations and an independent check of the pump.

CRUSH.clue: Mechanism and effect: instruction that is unsafe for extended-release, enteric, and hazardous tablets
CRUSH.rationale: Do-not-This drug lists include bupropion XL, bisacodyl, and many oncology drugs. Open a capsule only if the label allows it.

HAZARDOUS.clue: Mechanism and effect: drug category that includes chemotherapy and requires special handling
HAZARDOUS.rationale: This drug drugs are not crushed on an open counter. Pregnant staff follow the facility handling policy.

REMS.clue: Mechanism and effect: fDA program that restricts distribution of drugs with serious risks
REMS.rationale: Isotretinoin and clozapine are examples of drugs with required monitoring programs. A prescription alone may not be enough to dispense.

TRETINOIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: topical retinoid for acne that is photosensitizing and not the oral teratogen
TRETINOIN.rationale: Topical This drug is not isotretinoin. It still irritates skin and is avoided in pregnancy by many clinicians.

BENZOYL.clue: Mechanism and effect: topical antibacterial for acne that bleaches fabric
BENZOYL.rationale: This drug peroxide can inactivate tretinoin if they are applied at the same moment. Many regimens separate them.

ADAPALENE.clue: Mechanism and effect: topical retinoid available over the counter for acne
ADAPALENE.rationale: This drug causes dryness and sun sensitivity. Benefit takes weeks.

HYDROCORT.clue: Mechanism and effect: low-potency topical steroid safe enough for limited face and fold use
HYDROCORT.rationale: Hydrocortisone is the mild end of the topical steroid ladder. Potent steroids are not used on the face chronically.

CLOBETASOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: super-potent topical steroid limited to short courses
CLOBETASOL.rationale: This drug can thin skin and suppress the adrenal axis if it is used on large areas for long periods.

MUPIROCIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: topical antibiotic for impetigo and nasal decolonization
MUPIROCIN.rationale: This drug ointment is applied to lesions. The nasal form is for staph carriage protocols, not routine cuts.

LIDOCAINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: local anesthetic patch or gel with a maximum daily dose because of seizures and arrhythmias
LIDOCAINE.rationale: This drug patches are worn for 12 hours and off for 12. Do not cover them with heat.

CAPSAICIN.clue: Mechanism and effect: topical chili derivative for neuropathic pain that burns at first
CAPSAICIN.rationale: This drug is applied with gloves. Hands are washed so the drug is not transferred to the eyes.

MENTHOL.clue: Mechanism and effect: counterirritant in many topical pain products
MENTHOL.rationale: This drug feels cool. Combination patches still count toward the lidocaine or salicylate dose if those are included.

VARENICLINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: partial nicotine agonist for smoking cessation that can change mood
VARENICLINE.rationale: This drug is titrated to reduce nausea. Psychiatric history is discussed, and vivid dreams are common.

NICOTINE.clue: Mechanism and effect: replacement therapy that is not smoked and is dosed to withdrawal symptoms
NICOTINE.rationale: This drug gum is chewed and parked. The patch is removed at night if insomnia or vivid dreams occur.
